partial_weld_report.caption_latex: Acquisition geometry and independently prescribed LOF. Grey dots denote receivers and orange triangles the five source centres. Blue dashed rectangles show the identical primary imaging region. Panels (a,b) use an expanded vertical scale to show the change in acquisition height; lateral absorbers lie outside these panels. Panel (c) gives the partial-weld floor and both LOF tips. The grey internal fusion boundary is bonded outside the LOF.

Mode-dependent launch and normal-velocity reception for the 0.5--5 MHz band, with the common 20\% gate shown dotted. Curves are separately normalized and do not compare absolute L/S strength. Panel (c) shows the vertical floor-to-pixel round-trip example; the grey early-time region lacks complete FIR support. Actual admitted bistatic paths can have longer travel times.

Illustrative partial-weld ray geometry for all eight pure-S splits. Orange solid branches run from S1 at $(-1.5,16.4)$ mm to the fixed illustration point $(0,20.95)$ mm; blue dashed branches run to floor receiver R330 at approximately $(1.9402,16.4)$ mm. Triangles mark source and receiver; the black dot is the illustration point. Titles include the 0.030 \us\ trigger. Pure-L routes have the same geometry for these homogeneous pure-mode branches, but shorter times. Admission gates and FIR support are not encoded in this drawing; the direct $S\mid S$ example arrives too early for full FIR support.

Recording-level evidence for S1 and floor receiver R330. (a) Signed, band-filtered LOF/reference traces with predicted specimen-only backwall LL (3.113 \us), SS (5.690 \us) and repeated SSSS (11.199 \us) returns. (b) Analytic envelopes including waveform difference. Grey shading marks centres with incomplete early FIR support; traces there are displayed for explanation but excluded from imaging. (c) Whole-record raw Hann spectrum, individually normalized; shading denotes the imaging band. (d) All S1 receiver envelopes, with white gaps between measurement groups; the centre group lies 16.4 mm below the plate groups. B-scan 0 dB is 1449.18 \um/s and is separate from image normalization.

Partial-weld LOF-only images, candidates 1--9, with unchanged primary controls. Each panel states its supported global peak. The bar marks scattering at each image pixel; it is not an added physical interface. Cyan identifies known LOF; grey is unsupported. Every panel uses the same 60 dB range and 72.80565 \um/s reference as the companion atlas and the full-weld comparison.

Partial-weld LOF-only images, candidates 10--18, continuing the catalogue. Weak long-path images are not individually normalized upward. Small supported areas in the LLL-transmit paths should not be read as successful background suppression: no near-flaw pixels qualify in those two paths.

Matched partial-weld LOF, pristine-reference and signed waveform-difference controls for six diagnostic examples. Rows include the direct modes, the localizing reflected shear path, the misleading $L\mid LLL$ response, and two longer shear views. All 18 paths remain tabulated; these examples explain mechanisms rather than select settings. The common 0 dB reference is 73.56996 \um/s. The known-LOF overlay on the pristine panels is a coordinate guide only: those models contain no flaw.

Partial-weld receiver usage for all pure-S candidates. Colour is the fraction of supported final-image pixels at which each source/receiver pair contributes. Dashed boundaries separate IDs R0--R156 (left), R157--R313 (right) and R314--R330 (fill floor); ID order is not left--fill--right. S0/S4 are shoulder sources and S1--S3 are floor sources. The figure is a whole-grid aperture audit, not a flaw-centred receiver selection.

Selected partial-weld sensitivities, all evaluated at 0.2 mm spacing. (a) Change in $C_{99}$ relative to the coarse baseline. (b) Remaining near-flaw support. Grey dashes indicate undefined contrast rather than zero change. ``+ All echoes'' adds LL, LS/SL, SS and SSSS specimen-only screening. Improvements in contrast accompanied by lost coverage are not accepted as better settings.

All nine partial-weld wider-field diagnostics: eight pure-S paths and direct L. The reference and 60 dB range are shared across these panels and the full-weld wider-field comparison. White dashed rectangles mark the primary grid. White air is distinct from grey unsupported material. These 0.25 mm images give context over the receiver span; they do not imply whole-specimen coverage.

Waveform-difference images for candidates 1--9. These use the same settings and common control reference as the paired examples. Subtraction acts on signed recordings before nonlinear reconstruction, and can reveal changes in reverberation as well as scattering at the flaw.

Waveform-difference images for candidates 10--18. Missing support remains grey. Reference images for all candidates are supplied as separate publication figures in the editable bundle; their near-flaw amplitudes are tabulated in the main report.

combined_weld_report.caption_latex: Acquisition geometry and independently prescribed LOF. Grey dots denote receivers and orange triangles the five source centres. Blue dashed rectangles show the identical primary imaging region. Panels (a,b) use an expanded vertical scale to show the change in acquisition height; lateral absorbers lie outside these panels. Panel (c) gives the partial-weld floor and both LOF tips. The grey internal fusion boundary is bonded outside the LOF.

Paired primary results for all 18 paths. (a) Near-flaw peak relative to the 99th percentile of supported distant background. (b) Percentage of the geometric near-flaw tube with valid support. (c) Distance from the LOF segment to the global image maximum. Dashes denote undefined values. Colour scales are clipped for readability; printed numbers retain the measured values. Contrast alone must be read with support and peak location.

Full-weld LOF-only atlas, candidates 1--9. The primary region is the lower 8.6 mm comparison window, not the entire full-weld thickness. Titles identify the focusing split; annotations give the supported global maximum. The common reference is 72.80565 \um/s with 60 dB range. Cyan dashed LOF overlays and open tip markers do not determine the aperture.

Full-weld LOF-only atlas, candidates 10--18, with the same settings, reference and extent. Uniform grey panels have no supported pixels. The long-transmit LLL paths and much of the SSS-transmit family are strongly restricted in this acquisition.

Partial-weld LOF-only atlas, candidates 1--9, on exactly the same physical and dB scales as the full-weld panels. Bright floor-adjacent structures dominate several short-path images. $S\mid SS$ retains a localized maximum near the LOF under unchanged controls.

Partial-weld LOF-only atlas, candidates 10--18. Longer paths change support and background structure, but none in this half of the catalogue places its global maximum within 0.5 mm of the known flaw. Small valid regions and dark images must be distinguished from genuine background rejection.

Physical admission and early-time support. Launch and normal-reception curves use separately normalized modal magnitudes with the same 20\% threshold. The vertical timing example highlights the first 3.28 \us, which lack complete filter support. Longer bistatic or reflected routes can arrive outside this region even when a vertical direct echo cannot.

Fraction of supported final-image pixels at which each source qualifies, for every path and weld state. S0 and S4 are shoulders in both states. S1--S3 move from OD in full weld to fill floor in partial weld. Percentages are conditioned on supported pixels and do not sum to 100\%; several sources can qualify at one pixel. Dashes indicate no supported final-image pixels.

LOF-only score profiles on the same extended straight LOF line, with bilinear interpolation of the 0.1 mm arrays. Blue solid and orange dashed curves denote full and partial welds. Grey shading marks the actual tip-depth interval. Each panel uses physical score units, not independent peak normalization; scales differ between panels. NaN gaps retain missing support. Profiles are diagnostic and were not used to tune settings.

Partial-weld controls illustrating strong structural background and defect-associated changes. Rows are six diagnostic examples; all candidates are retained quantitatively. LOF, reference and waveform difference share the same 73.56996 \um/s reference and 60 dB range. The cyan overlay in pristine models denotes the location at which the flaw would be present, not an actual separation.

Wider-field comparison for direct S, direct L and $S\mid SS$, at 0.25 mm spacing. Full and partial panels share 0 dB = 53.87031 \um/s and 60 dB range. White air and grey missing support are distinct from low-amplitude black. White dashed rectangles indicate the primary lower-weld comparison region. This field covers the receiver span, not the entire 150 mm numerical specimen.

Wider-field comparison for $SS\mid S$, $SS\mid SS$ and $SSS\mid SS$, using the same scale as the preceding figure. Lateral near-surface artefacts can exceed the primary-region flaw response. Cropping or independently normalizing a path can conceal these competing maxima.
